knobs.label: keep_warm idle tail (x session hours)
knobs.why: Beam bills a sandbox until terminate() or until its keep_warm_seconds TTL expires. The SDK default TTL is 600 s (10 min) when keep_warm_seconds is not set, so a sandbox that is never terminate()d bills a 10-minute idle tail; -1 never expires; docs examples use 30 min-2 h. Factor = (session + TTL) / session; 1 = explicit terminate().

caveats: CPU is priced per physical core = 2 vCPU; vcpu_h is the per-core price / 2. The SDK documents cpu= as "The number of CPU cores allocated to the container. Default is 1.0" (default memory 128 MiB), so cpu=1 = 1 billed core = 2 vCPU as priced. Whether a 'core' in the SDK is a full physical core (2 hyperthreads) is not stated explicitly.
Dated price change: Beam blogs of June 2026 quote sandbox CPU $0.0000528/core-s ($0.19/core-h) and RAM $0.0000056/GB-s; current page $0.0000375 and $0.0000064 (CPU -29%, RAM +14%).
Sandbox CPU/RAM are 3x the serverless container rate (alt mode). The page's cost calculator uses the serverless rate, not the sandbox rate.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.note: Sandboxes terminate when keep_warm_seconds expires; no pause/sleep with state capture is documented, snapshots are explicit SDK calls. Only exception: attached DurableDisks are snapshotted to object storage on container stop ('Beam snapshots a disk to object storage each time the container using it stops', https://docs.beam.cloud/v2/data/durable-disks.md). That is disk-only persistence of an extra attached disk, not the sandbox's state, so not counted here.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: You can also create a memory snapshot of a running Sandbox, which will capture the state of the sandbox's memory - including all running processes and exposed ports.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Two kinds: create_image_from_filesystem() (filesystem -> image id usable as base image for any Sandbox/app) and snapshot_memory() (memory + processes + exposed ports; SDK docstring says also GPU state). New sandboxes boot from them via Image.from_id / Sandbox().create_from_memory_snapshot(), i.e. fork. Snapshots are free per pricing page.

harness_api.quote: A sandboxed container for running Python code or arbitrary processes.
harness_api.note: The Sandbox SDK exposes only process exec/run_code, filesystem, ports, snapshots, network, Docker. No API to start/stream/resume Claude Code/Codex/etc. Beam's 'agents' docs are a petri-net agent framework, and the new MCP server (beta9 PR #1920/#1942) lets an outside agent drive Beam (deploy, pods, secrets), not a harness running inside a sandbox. 'Managed agents' in commits are Beam's worker-machine agents.

egress_allowlist.quote: For more fine-grained control, you can specify an allow list of CIDR ranges that your Sandbox is permitted to connect to. All other outbound traffic will be blocked.
egress_allowlist.note: block_network=True (no outbound) or allow_list of max 10 CIDRs (IPv4/IPv6), no hostnames. Updatable at runtime via update_network_permissions() without restart. Same for Pods.

egress_http_rules.quote: Must use proper CIDR notation (e.g., "8.8.8.8/32" for a single IP, "10.0.0.0/8" for a range)
egress_http_rules.note: Only CIDR-level egress controls are documented; nothing at HTTP method/path/header level.

ingress_rules.quote: Whether the sandbox should be authorized for external access. Default is False.
ingress_rules.note: You choose which ports are exposed (ports=[...] at creation or expose_port() at runtime); exposed ports get SSL-terminated public URLs (https://<id>-<port>.app.beam.cloud). The SDK has an `authorized` flag (default False) which, as for Beam endpoints/pods, appears to require the Beam bearer token when True; the sandbox docs page itself does not document it. No IP allowlists for inbound. Pods are served from a static IP range (on request).

secret_proxy.quote: You can attach secrets to your sandbox using Beam's secret management system - they will be exposed as environment variables inside the Sandbox
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are only env vars inside the container; no credential-injecting egress proxy documented.

volume_attach.quote: Mount fast storage volumes to persist files between sessions
volume_attach.note: Three kinds attachable to a Sandbox: distributed Volumes, CloudBucket (your S3-compatible bucket), DurableDisk (node-local SSD snapshotted to object storage, 'The `disks` parameter is accepted by ... Sandbox'). Volumes free to 1 TB then $0.021/GB-month.

volume_shared.quote: If several containers need to read and write the same files at the same time, use a [Volume](/v2/data/volume) instead. Volumes are shared, distributed storage.
volume_shared.note: Volumes are read-write shared across containers/sandboxes (writes visible to others within ~60 s); CloudBuckets also shared. DurableDisks: one writer at a time, any number of read-only mounts.

nested_virt.quote: Each workload runs in its own container as a non-root user, isolated from other customers' workloads.
nested_virt.note: Sandboxes run as gVisor-isolated, non-root containers (card isolation: gvisor). No /dev/kvm or nested-virtualization capability is documented anywhere in the SDK/docs; a gVisor container sandbox does not expose hardware virtualization to the guest. not offered: outside the product's scope.

anti_bot.quote: Sandboxes are ultra-fast, Python-native environments for running any workload - with GPUs, networking, and persistent storage - in seconds.
anti_bot.note: Beam is a serverless compute/sandbox platform for running code, GPUs and containers; it has no browser (browser=false) or managed-browser product, so stealth/fingerprinting-evasion against bot detection is not offered. not offered: outside the product's scope.

captcha_solving.quote: Sandboxes are ultra-fast, Python-native environments for running any workload - with GPUs, networking, and persistent storage - in seconds.
captcha_solving.note: No browser/computer-use product exists on Beam (browser=false, desktop=false); built-in CAPTCHA solving is not part of a general-purpose compute/sandbox platform. not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: Pods are served in a static IP range, making it possible to whitelist the Beam IP range from the client.
egress_ip_type.note: Outbound traffic comes from AWS/GCP datacenter ranges (security page: infrastructure on AWS/GCP). Documented explicitly as a fixed/static IP range for Pods (contact Beam for the range); Sandbox docs don't repeat this, but sandboxes share the same network egress path, so a fixed datacenter range is the best-supported answer rather than plain rotating datacenter IPs.

fork_running.quote: You can also create a memory snapshot of a running Sandbox, which will capture the state of the sandbox's memory - including all running processes and exposed ports.
fork_running.note: The docs example calls sandbox.snapshot_memory() on a sandbox that is still running (a server process is executing and a port is exposed) and only calls terminate() afterward; the snapshot is not preceded by stopping the sandbox. The resulting snapshot can be used via create_from_memory_snapshot() to clone a new sandbox with processes/state intact, i.e. forking a running machine without stopping it.

wake_on_request.note: For the Sandbox product (this card's primary mode), a sandbox that hits its keep_warm_seconds TTL (or is terminate()d) is gone; there is no documented mechanism for an external request to automatically wake/recreate a terminated sandbox with its prior state (memory snapshots must be explicitly restored via create_from_memory_snapshot()). This matches the card's own mode-level features (auto_stop_idle sandbox modes: wake_on_request=false). Beam's separate serverless containers (Endpoints/pods, an alt/paas mode) do scale from zero on an incoming request (wake_on_request=true there), but that is a different product surface than the Sandbox.

live_resize.note: The SandboxInstance API only exposes expose_port(), list_urls(), update_network_permissions(), update_ttl(), terminate(), create_image_from_filesystem(), snapshot_memory() -- no update_cpu/update_memory/resize method. The configuration docs tell users to create a new, bigger sandbox instead of resizing ('If you need more power, create a new sandbox'), confirming CPU/RAM cannot be changed on a running sandbox.

own_agent_api.quote: Beam is launching a new type of agent framework that is stateful and has concurrency built-in.
own_agent_api.note: Beam's 'agents' feature is a petri-net orchestration framework (Bot/BotLocation/BotContext) for building YOUR OWN agents on top of Beam compute -- it is not a first-party API that drives a Beam-owned browser/computer-use/research agent. Beam has no browser or desktop product. not offered: outside the product's scope.

lang_node.quote:
Running a Node.js server
You can run arbitrary code on Beam. It doesn't need to be Python!
... sb = Sandbox(image=Image().from_registry("node:20")).create()
lang_node.note: Node.js is a documented first-class quickstart runtime for Sandboxes (via image), and Beam additionally ships a first-party TypeScript SDK (@beamcloud/beam-js) to drive Sandboxes/Pods/etc. from Node.js code.

guest_firewall.quote: Each workload runs in its own container as a non-root user, isolated from other customers' workloads.
guest_firewall.note: derived: this is a gVisor container sandbox, not a full VM/microVM, and root=false (non-root user), so nftables/iptables inside the guest are not expected to work reliably; outbound network policy is instead enforced provider-side via allow_list/block_network (egress_allowlist).

static_egress_ip.quote: Pods are served in a static IP range, making it possible to whitelist the Beam IP range from the client.
static_egress_ip.note: Documented for Pods only ('For the static IP range, send us a message in Slack'): a fixed/static range rather than a dedicated single IP per machine, and Sandbox docs do not repeat this claim explicitly, but it indicates Beam's egress infrastructure uses a stable, whitelistable IP range rather than fully arbitrary rotating IPs.

eu_data_residency.quote: Customer workloads run in the United States unless you choose a specific region or compute pool where the platform offers one.
eu_data_residency.note: Confirms customers can opt into a specific region (the card's regions include 'eu') for workload placement, i.e. EU data residency is available on request, consistent with the card's note that EU/Asia placement is available by contacting Beam.

root.quote: $ beam shell app.py:handler ... Welcome to Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (GNU/Linux 6.8.0-51-generic x86_64) root@runc:/mnt/code#
root.note: Beam's own CLI reference shows `beam shell` dropping you into a root@ prompt inside the container. This contradicts the security page's marketing line ('runs in its own container as a non-root user') and the card's root:false; the CLI transcript is the concrete, user-facing behavior, so root should be true.

pause_resume.quote: SandboxInstance.terminate() Terminate the container associated with this sandbox instance.
pause_resume.note: The SDK exposes only create()/terminate() (plus a keep_warm_seconds TTL and update_ttl()); there is no stop/pause/suspend call that freezes a running sandbox and later resumes it at reduced/no cost. The configuration docs' phrase 'pause and resume work' is just marketing for setting keep_warm_seconds=-1 (manual termination), not a real pause API - confirms no.

desktop.quote: Beam lets you run functions, REST APIs, task queues, and sandboxes on CPUs and GPUs, end to end.
desktop.note: Not offered: outside the product's scope. Beam is a code-execution/serverless-compute sandbox (process exec, filesystem, ports, GPUs); no VNC/RDP/graphical desktop is mentioned anywhere in the docs.

browser.quote: Beam lets you run functions, REST APIs, task queues, and sandboxes on CPUs and GPUs, end to end.
browser.note: Not offered: outside the product's scope. No managed/real browser is bundled or offered; the docs' web-scraping example just installs whatever scraping library the user chooses inside a plain Linux container.

computer_use.quote: Beam lets you run functions, REST APIs, task queues, and sandboxes on CPUs and GPUs, end to end.
computer_use.note: Not offered: outside the product's scope. No screenshot+click desktop-driving API exists; Beam's 'agents' page is a petri-net task-orchestration framework, not a computer-use API.

public_ipv4.quote: url = sb.expose_port(8000) ... The URL will be something like: https://384ced3c-f837-4429-bada-39e0b965c9f4-8000.app.beam.cloud
public_ipv4.note: Sandboxes are reached only via SSL-terminated *.app.beam.cloud hostnames, not an assigned public IPv4 address. (Pods separately sit behind a shared static outbound IP range on request, but that's egress, not a per-machine public IPv4 - docs.beam.cloud/v2/pod/networking.md: 'Pods are served in a static IP range'.) Confirms no.

agent_harnesses.note: The only Claude/Cursor integration is adding Beam's own documentation as an MCP tool inside a local Claude Code/Cursor session on the user's machine - not a preinstalled coding-agent template running inside a Beam sandbox. No page offers Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode as a sandbox template.

windows.quote: You can install Beam on Windows using Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL).
windows.note: The only 'Windows' mention is running the local Beam CLI on a developer's Windows machine via WSL; the remote sandbox/container itself is Linux only (Ubuntu 22.04, per the CLI shell transcript). Not offered: outside the product's scope.

macos.quote: Beam lets you run functions, REST APIs, task queues, and sandboxes on CPUs and GPUs, end to end.
macos.note: Not offered: outside the product's scope. Beam runs customer workloads on AWS/GCP Linux infrastructure (docs.beam.cloud/v2/security/security.md: 'Beam runs on infrastructure provided by Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud'); no macOS machine type exists.

arm64.note: No architecture flag or ARM/aarch64/Graviton option appears anywhere in the docs (custom-images, custom-registries, resources, py-sdk); base images and GPU examples are all standard x86_64 (CUDA) images, and the CLI shell transcript shows 'x86_64'. Treated as not offered.

sso.quote: All members of a workspace currently have the same permissions, and single sign-on is not yet available; remove members and rotate tokens when someone leaves your team.
sso.note: Explicit first-party statement that SSO is not yet available. Confirms no.

max_session_h.note: No published hard cap on sandbox lifetime. keep_warm_seconds=-1 lets a sandbox run until you explicitly terminate() it ('Use manual termination for: Long-running training jobs, Collaborative development sessions, When you need to pause and resume work'). Docs/pricing/FAQ pages re-checked 2026-09-30 have no mention of a maximum session duration or forced eviction time, consistent with the card's own caveat 'Max sandbox size and max lifetime unpublished.' Treated as no limit rather than null since the platform explicitly supports indefinite manual-only termination.

usage_api.quote: Metrics endpoints (GET /metrics/{ws}/stub-timeseries, workspace-timeseries, pool-timeseries) return resource time series (CPU, memory, GPU, network) but not billable usage units or costs. Billing is visible in the dashboard only; no programmatic billing/cost API is documented.
usage_api.note: granularity: none; cost: no; Beam exposes metrics for monitoring (CPU/memory/GPU/network per container) via REST API and logs/task status endpoints, but no dedicated billing usage API that returns billable quantities (CPU-hours, RAM-hours, GPU-hours) or cost per sandbox/tag/project. Usage is only accessible through the account dashboard.
